headline: Indian markets slip as RBI rate hike and global hawkish cues weigh on investor sentiment

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: RBI hiked interest rates for the first time in nearly four years amid ongoing price pressures.
US Fed minutes signaled another rate hike by year-end as US Treasury yields climbed higher.
Foreign investors pulled out $26.3 billion from emerging markets in September due to a hawkish Fed policy outlook.
Global market weakness and rising US yields triggered selling pressure across major domestic sectors.
whatHappening: Sensex ended 429 points lower while Nifty closed near the 22,600 mark following the central bank's rate decision.
Hindalco dropped 3% and Infosys fell 2%, featuring among the leading losers in recent trading.
Adani Enterprises and Hindalco were highlighted among the top losing stocks on the market.
An IndiGo Patna-Lucknow flight landed safely after its nose was damaged by a mid-air lightning strike.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices closed lower as Sensex fell 429 points and Nifty slipped to near 22,600 following an RBI rate hike.
Hawkish US Fed rate expectations and rising Treasury yields led to foreign investor capital outflows from emerging markets.
Major equities including Hindalco, Infosys, and Adani Enterprises recorded losses amidst broader market selling pressure.
